idiom_name: newtype envelope over Box<dyn Letter> (trait object), with explicit or Deref forwarding
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance, so the letter interface is a trait and the letter is a trait object: the envelope is a newtype struct holding Box<dyn Letter> (or Arc<dyn Letter + Send + Sync> when the letter is shared across threads), forwarding either with explicit methods or through a Deref implementation that makes the envelope look like the letter. Dynamic dispatch through the vtable blocks inlining exactly as in the C++ original, so the same performance trade applies; when the set of letters is closed, an enum with match gives static dispatch and exhaustive checking instead, which is the sealed-hierarchy replacement rather than this pattern. Explicit forwarding is preferred for published APIs because Deref hides which methods belong to the envelope.
pitfalls: The trait must be dyn-compatible (object safe): generic methods, methods returning Self and associated constants disqualify it from dyn, which often forces a clone_letter() style method instead of a Clone bound.
Box<dyn Letter> defaults to a 'static trait object, so a letter that borrows data needs an explicit lifetime parameter - and the envelope then carries that lifetime through every signature.

Deriving Clone on the envelope clones the Box, which does not compile for a trait object; the deep copy must go through the letter's own clone method, and Deref plus inherent methods with the same name can silently shadow each other.
